headline: A large spending law that funds seven federal departments and agencies for fiscal year 2019 and adds several immigration extensions and technical fixes.
what_it_does: This law provides fiscal year 2019 money for seven of the twelve regular spending bills, covering areas such as Homeland Security, agriculture and food safety, commerce and justice, financial services, the Interior and environment, foreign aid and diplomacy, and transportation and housing. It sets many rules on how that money may be used, such as limits on overtime, contract oversight, and certain transfers between accounts. It also extends several expiring immigration programs through fiscal year 2019 and makes various technical changes to current law.

who_it_affects.group: Federal employees at agencies such as Customs and Border Protection, ICE, and the Secret Service
who_it_affects.how: Their overtime pay is limited in most cases unless the agency determines an exception is needed.

who_it_affects.group: Immigrants and employers who use the E-Verify system
who_it_affects.how: The E-Verify employment eligibility program is extended through fiscal year 2019.

who_it_affects.group: Foreign doctors on J-1 visas who work in medically underserved areas
who_it_affects.how: The Conrad 30 waiver program is extended through fiscal year 2019.

who_it_affects.group: Foreign investors and regional economic projects using the EB-5 program
who_it_affects.how: The Regional Center Pilot Program is extended through fiscal year 2019.
The law provides funding for rural development, broadband pilot programs, and farm programs, and it sets rules for certain loans and grants.

who_it_affects.group: Students and families in the school lunch and school breakfast programs
who_it_affects.how: Some lunch pricing rules are changed for the 2019-2020 school year, and some school breakfast rule changes are blocked.

who_it_affects.group: Federal Medicare and Medicaid beneficiaries and others who rely on SNAP food assistance
who_it_affects.how: The law sets rules for SNAP retailer stocking requirements and provides money for the SNAP program during fiscal year 2019.

who_it_affects.group: Taxpayers who deal with the IRS
who_it_affects.how: The law sets requirements for IRS taxpayer service, identity theft protection, and confidentiality of tax information.
The law provides a pay increase for federal employees and funds for retirement and health benefit payments.

when_it_takes_effect: Most provisions apply to fiscal year 2019, which runs from October 1, 2018 through September 30, 2019, and the law was enacted on February 15, 2019.
